title: Egypt’s royal tomb builders staged one of history’s first strikes
body: Around 1158 BC, in the 29th year of Ramesses III’s reign, the artisans of Deir el-Medina, who cut and decorated the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, put down their tools because their grain rations had not arrived. They staged sit-ins at temples and told officials, ‘We are hungry’. Grain was released, and the dispute was written down on a papyrus now kept in Turin.

steps.label: The tomb builders put down their tools

slides.question: Why did the tomb builders of Deir el-Medina put down their tools?
options: Their grain rations had not arrived
A new pharaoh cancelled their tombs
slides.explanation: In the 29th year of Ramesses III, around 1158 BC, the artisans’ grain rations failed to arrive. They staged sit-ins at temples, telling officials ‘We are hungry’, and grain was released.

slides.clue: The writing material, now kept in Turin, on which the dispute was recorded
slides.detail: The so-called Strike Papyrus, written by Amunnakht and now in Turin, records the sit-ins and complaints of the 29th year of Ramesses III.
